hello.note: Works any time of day, and is also a casual goodbye

good-morning.text: ສະບາຍດີຕອນເຊົ້າ
good-morning.note: Most people just say sabaidee all day

please.note: Formal. In a shop people usually say ຂໍ (kaw) before the item

thank-you.note: ຂອບໃຈຫຼາຍໆ (kawp jai lai lai) means thank you very much

yes.note: Literally "it is". ເຈົ້າ (jao) is also used as a polite yes

no.note: ບໍ່ແມ່ນ (baw men) means "no, it isn't"

dont-understand.text: ຂ້ອຍບໍ່ເຂົ້າໃຈ

speak-slowly.text: ກະລຸນາເວົ້າຊ້າໆ
speak-slowly.note: Saying a word twice, as in sah sah, softens it

repeat.text: ກະລຸນາເວົ້າອີກເທື່ອໜຶ່ງ

speak-english.text: ເຈົ້າເວົ້າພາສາອັງກິດໄດ້ບໍ
speak-english.say: jao wow pa-sa ang-git dai baw
speak-english.note: Ending with ບໍ (baw) makes it a yes/no question. ເຈົ້າ (jao) means you

thousand.note: Prices are in kip and run into the thousands: ພັນ (pan) is a thousand, ແສນ (saen) a hundred thousand, ລ້ານ (lan) a million

how-much.note: Point at the item and say ອັນນີ້ເທົ່າໃດ (an nee tow dai), how much is this?

would-like.note: Literally "I request …"; the normal polite way to ask for something

i-want.text: ຂ້ອຍຢາກໄດ້…

do-you-have.note: Put the item in the gap

just-looking.text: ຂ້ອຍພຽງແຕ່ເບິ່ງ

ill-take-it.text: ເອົາອັນນີ້

discount.text: ຫຼຸດລາຄາໄດ້ບໍ
discount.note: Bargaining is normal in markets, not in fixed-price shops

card.text: ຮັບບັດເຄຣດິດບໍ
card.note: Cash is still common: kip, and often Thai baht or US dollars

reservation.text: ຂ້ອຍຈອງຫ້ອງໄວ້ແລ້ວ

checkout-time.text: ເຊັກເອົາຈັກໂມງ

breakfast.text: ລວມອາຫານເຊົ້າບໍ

wifi.text: ລະຫັດວາຍຟາຍແມ່ນຫຍັງ

toilet.text: ຫ້ອງນ້ຳຢູ່ໃສ
toilet.note: "… ຢູ່ໃສ (yoo sai)" means "where is …?" for anything

taxi.text: ຊ່ວຍເອີ້ນແທັກຊີໃຫ້ໄດ້ບໍ
taxi.say: soo-ay urn tak-see hai dai baw
taxi.note: Tuk-tuks (ຕຸກຕຸກ) are more common than taxis

allergic.note: Add the food, or show a note written in Lao to be safe
